name: exocean
description: exocean is an experimental oceanology laboratory at CEREGE, Aix-en-Provence, founded by CNRS scientists studying the ocean's role in the global carbon cycle.

home.title: Who We Are
home.lede: – Exocean, bringing the ocean inside the lab.
intro: We are an Oceanology Laboratory founded by CNRS scientists with complementary expertise, united by the shared goal of better understanding the ocean's role in the global carbon cycle. Our work combines innovation, curiosity, and a collaborative spirit to develop new tools and insights into ocean systems.
Together, the team is developing a shared research framework around the ocean carbonate system — one that connects surface ecosystems, deep-sea feedbacks, and sedimentary records.
home.founders_caption: Thomas B. CHALK, Olivier SULPIS and Julie MEILLAND, exocean founders (CEREGE) / Photo © Elodie GAZQUEZ, 2025.
home.founders_intro: At the centre of the project, we are three researchers whose approaches bridge biology, geochemistry, and sedimentary processes:

founders.name: Thomas CHALK
founders.blurb: Resident geochemist and ERC awardee for the ForCry project, I am developing laser ablation techniques for the miniaturisation of sample analysis through novel techniques. I specialise in the reconstruction of past ocean pH and CO₂ at high spatial and temporal scales.

founders.name: Olivier SULPIS
founders.blurb: Carbonate cycle expert and ERC grantee behind the Deep-C project, I explore deep-sea carbonate dissolution under high pressure, in the laboratory, to unveil how marine sediments act as a long-term CO₂ sink and contribute to Earth's climate regulation.

founders.name: Julie MEILLAND
founders.blurb: Specialist in planktonic foraminifera reproduction and in vitro culture. My work — ranging from cultured experiments to field-based studies — helps clarify the living conditions and carbon export role of these key calcifying organisms, contributing essential knowledge on the biological carbon pump.

home.questions_title: Our key questions span from surface to deep-sea:
questions: What controls spatial variability in oceanic carbon fluxes?
How are carbon fluxes impacted by calcifying plankton population dynamics?
What is the future of ocean biogenic carbon production and export?
How sensitive is climate change to initial climate conditions?
How do deep-sea processes mitigate anthropogenic CO₂?
And how are human activities already leaving traces in the sediment record?
where: We are based at CEREGE (Centre for Research and Teaching in Environmental Geosciences), a multidisciplinary research and teaching center covering a broad range of scientific topics at the highest level, supported by state-of-the-art analytical facilities. It is one of the leading Earth Science laboratories in France and internationally recognized for its scientific excellence.

Ideally located in the heart of the Technopôle de l'Arbois in Aix-en-Provence and in central Marseille on the Saint-Charles campus, CEREGE benefits from optimal conditions to foster collaborations and partnerships.
Within CEREGE, exocean is one of the laboratories of the Experimental Biophysics and Chemistry technical centre — see how it fits in, and the other platforms you can use during a visit.

data.title: Data & Models
data.lede: - Models, datasets and tools we build and share — all open and free to use.
data.intro: Write to us if you use them, get stuck, or would like something that is not listed.

items.name: RADI
items.sub: Reaction-transport model of early diagenesis in marine sediments
items.body: The reactive-advective-diffusive-irrigative model simulates, through time, the chemistry of surface sediments and their exchanges with the overlying seawater, in Julia (Radi.jl) and MATLAB/GNU Octave (Radi.m). RADIv2 handles coastal and open-ocean sediments alike.

items.name: FORCIS
items.sub: Global census of living planktonic foraminifera
items.body: Distribution and diversity of planktonic foraminifera from a century of plankton-net, pump, sediment-trap and continuous-plankton-recorder samples across the world ocean, with an R package to download, filter, harmonise and map the data.

items.name: Cenozoic CO₂ (CenCO2PIP)
items.sub: 66 million years of atmospheric CO₂ from proxy records
items.body: A community-vetted synthesis of atmospheric CO₂ over the Cenozoic, assembled by the Cenozoic CO₂ Proxy Integration Project consortium from marine and terrestrial proxy records. Every record and its evaluation is openly archived.

items.name: Micro-CT images of planktonic foraminifera
items.sub: 3D scans of shells with curated taxonomy
items.body: X-ray micro-computed tomography images of 179 shells covering 43 of the 48 recognised species and subspecies of holoplanktonic foraminifera, with their metadata.

data.outro: All our articles, with open-access PDFs where they exist, are on the Publications page.

services.title: Services & Instruments
services.lede: - Analyses and experiments we run for partners, and the equipment behind them.
services.hero_alt: Planktonic foraminifera under the microscope, and Julie Meilland at a culture incubator in the exocean laboratory
services.hero_caption: Planktonic foraminifera under the microscope (top) and Julie MEILLAND preparing cultures in the exocean laboratory at CEREGE.
intro: Beyond our own research, we run measurements and experiments for academic and private partners — within a collaboration, or as a paid service. You can send us your samples, or come and work with us in the laboratory; visitors pay a small lab occupation fee.

exocean is part of CEREGE's network of technical platforms, so a stay with us can be combined with analyses on other CEREGE platforms — stable isotopes, elemental chemistry, X-ray imaging, micropalaeontology and more.

request.title: How to request an analysis
request.body: Write to us at {email} with a few lines on your samples (type, number, volume) and on what you need. We will tell you what is feasible and how long it will take, and send a quote for paid services. If you would also like to use other CEREGE platforms during your visit, say so and we will put you in touch.

offers.title: Seawater carbonate chemistry
offers.body: Total alkalinity by potentiometric titration on samples down to 4 mL, and pH by spectrophotometry with purified indicator dye. Alkalinity is calibrated with Dickson certified reference materials.

offers.title: Dissolved silicate and phosphate
offers.body: Silicate and phosphate concentrations in seawater, by colorimetry on a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.

offers.title: Microsensor profiling
offers.body: Microprofiles of oxygen, pH, nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide through sediments and other confined environments — in the lab, on ships right after sediment collection, or at coastal sites.

offers.title: Sediment–water interface experiments
offers.body: Sediment incubations in six temperature-controlled reactors that reproduce benthic hydrodynamics, from calm abyssal plains to reefs. Open or closed to the atmosphere, in free drift or flow-through, with chemistry followed in the porewaters and the overlying water.

offers.title: High-pressure incubations
offers.body: Water or solid samples held at up to 500 bar (roughly the pressure at 5,000 m depth) in a 600 mL vessel, with water sampling during the run. Gas composition cannot be measured with the current setup.

offers.title: Cultures and incubations
offers.body: Culture of plankton, microbes and other small organisms, and incubation experiments, under controlled temperature and light — from 0 to above 35 °C in the incubators of our COREFF foraminifera facility. Light intensity and spectrum are measured with a PAR sensor.
offers.note: COREFF, our COntinuous REproduction for Foraminifera Facility, can host thousands of planktonic foraminifera at a time — mostly Mediterranean species, kept alive and reproducing with protocols we keep refining — alongside diatom strains grown as food for their different life stages. For live specimens, visits or the culture season, contact Julie MEILLAND ().

offers.title: Respiration of single organisms
offers.body: Respiration of microbes, single foraminifera or other small plankton, measured with microsensors in very small volumes of water under a stereomicroscope.

offers.title: Microscopy and imaging
offers.body: Observation and imaging of living plankton and other immersed samples on an inverted microscope, and of small samples under a stereomicroscope.

offers.title: Plasma cleaning of samples
offers.body: Removal of organic matter from samples by plasma cleaning.

cerege.title: exocean within CEREGE
body: CEREGE groups its analytical and experimental facilities by area of expertise into six technical centres, each co-led by a technical and a scientific manager. exocean is one of the four laboratories of the Experimental Biophysics and Chemistry centre (technical manager Pierre Boutet, scientific manager Julie Meilland), together with the CIRENE technology hall, the colloid characterisation laboratory and the geomicrobiology laboratory.
cerege.platforms_title: Combine your visit with other CEREGE platforms
cerege.platforms_intro: The platforms most often useful to our partners. Each one has its own access conditions and rates — we can put you in touch.

platforms.name: PANISS
platforms.desc: δ¹⁸O and δ¹³C of carbonates, clumped isotopes (Δ<sub>47</sub>, Δ<sub>48</sub>), δ¹⁸O, δ¹⁷O and δD of water, and δ¹⁵N, δ¹³C and δD of organic compounds. Open to academic collaborations and services.

platforms.name: LA-ICP-MS
platforms.desc: About 90% of the periodic table in solution by ICP-OES or ICP-MS, and laser ablation of solids for semi-quantitative elemental maps. Open to public and private users.

platforms.name: LGO2i
platforms.desc: Radiocarbon dating on the AixMICADAS accelerator mass spectrometer, organic compounds as environmental indicators, and the elemental composition of marine and lake sediment archives.

platforms.name: MATRIX
platforms.desc: Micro- and nano-tomography, X-ray micro-diffraction and micro-XRF mapping of the same sample, all non-destructive. Open to all.

platforms.name: MANTA
platforms.desc: Automated microscopes with AI recognition of coccolithophores, foraminifera, radiolarians, diatoms and pollen, and a robot that picks foraminifera for chemical analyses.

platforms.name: LPM
platforms.desc: Extraction of microfossils and other bio-indicators from sediments, soils, plants and water samples, ready for microscopy or geochemistry.

platforms.name: SEDIM
platforms.desc: High-resolution imaging with mosaics, grain-size and particle-shape distributions (with or without chemical pre-treatment), and identification of micro- and macro-remains such as shells and ostracods.

services.instruments_intro: The equipment of the exocean laboratory at CEREGE, by type.

items.name: Metrohm OMNIS titrator
items.desc: Total alkalinity of seawater by potentiometric titration, on small volumes.

items.name: Agilent Cary 60 UV-Vis spectrophotometer
items.desc: Seawater chemistry by spectrophotometry: pH with purified indicator dye, dissolved silicate and phosphate.

items.name: Unisense microsensor profiling system
items.desc: Microsensors for oxygen, pH, nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide on a motorized, automated vertical micromanipulator.

items.name: Büchiglas Novoclave high-pressure reactor
items.desc: 600 mL vessel for water or solid samples, up to 500 bar.

items.name: Rotating disk reactors (×6)
items.desc: Stirred or rotating-disk reactors that reproduce benthic hydrodynamics, with chemical monitoring.

items.name: Unisense NanoRespiration system
items.desc: Incubation of microbes or plankton in very small volumes of water, followed with microsensors.

items.name: Friocell 111 EVO (×2) and Memmert incubators
items.desc: Culture of microbes, plankton and other small organisms, and incubations, under controlled temperature and light.

items.name: Zeiss Axiovert 5 inverted microscope
items.desc: Observation and imaging of living plankton and other immersed samples.

items.name: Zeiss Stemi 508 stereomicroscope
items.desc: Observation of samples and of microsensor tips.

items.name: PAR sensor
items.desc: Light intensity and spectrum in cultures and incubations.

items.name: Julabo CORIO refrigerated circulator
items.desc: Heating or cooling of reactors and incubations.

items.name: Henniker HPT-100 plasma cleaner
items.desc: Removal of organic matter from samples.

groups.heading: Reserved for the ERC Deep-C project
groups.note: Built for Deep-C and used only for that project; not available for other projects or for service work.

items.name: High-pressure reactors
items.desc: Abyssal to hadal pressures (up to 1000 bar), temperature-controlled, with water sampling under pressure.

items.name: Oxygen and pH meters
items.desc: Oxygen and pH monitoring in the high-pressure reactors.

contact.title: Let's connect!
contact.lede: - Curious to learn more about our work or explore a potential collaboration?
contact.body: We'd love to exchange ideas! Whether you're a researcher, partner institution, or simply intrigued by our projects, feel free to reach out.

join.title: Join us
join.lede: - Students, early-career researchers and visiting scientists are welcome all year round.

items.title: Internships
items.body: We host Master's and undergraduate interns every year, usually for two to six months, on topics ranging from foraminifera culture and microscopy to carbonate chemistry, high-pressure experiments and sediment reactors. Write to us with a CV and a few lines on what you would like to learn — we can usually shape a project together.

items.title: PhD and postdoctoral positions
items.body: Funded positions are announced on our Bluesky account as they open. We are also glad to hear from candidates who would like to prepare a fellowship application with us (Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions and similar schemes). Send a CV, a short statement of interests and the name of the team member whose work is closest to yours.

items.title: Visiting scientists and facility access
items.body: Colleagues who would like to run experiments with live planktonic foraminifera at COREFF, use our 500-bar reactor or the rotating disk reactors, or spend time in the laboratory can contact Julie MEILLAND (cultures) or Olivier SULPIS (reactors) directly; visitors pay a small lab occupation fee. Analyses we can run for you are listed on our Services page.
